title: Homes for Ukraine Share public-platform exit and continuing-operation receipt candidate
question: Does the official Homes for Ukraine record establish a completed exit from the former supplier platform and continuing public operation of Share, while preserving the unresolved migration-assurance, residual-custody, successor-dependency, affected-party-governance, and value-reconciliation deficits?

receipt.title: Homes for Ukraine Foundry-to-Share exit, public code custody, and continuing-operation record

claim_binding.identity_scope: The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government as controller and service owner; Palantir as the former supplier-platform provider; Share Homes for Ukraine data as the replacement service; local authorities and devolved administrations as operating users; Made Tech as a current technical-support processor; London-hosted cloud infrastructure as the current hosting layer; and Homes for Ukraine guests and sponsors as affected people.
claim_binding.temporal_scope: The emergency supplier deployment and contracts recorded from March 2022 through September 2023; the in-house build begun in summer 2024; delivery and supplier exit in September 2025; continuing operating guidance, privacy notice, grant conditions, public releases, and source-code maintenance through 17 August 2026.
claim_binding.predicate_scope: Whether MHCLG replaced the former supplier platform with a service it can operate and modify, whether operational continuity and public code custody are observed, which successor supplier and cloud dependencies remain, and whether independent migration assurance, residual-custody reconciliation, affected-party governance, and independently measured value recovery are established.
claim_binding.claim: Official records establish that MHCLG began building Share in summer 2024, migrated three years of operational data, delivered the service in September 2025, exited the former supplier contract, and continued operating and modifying Share through at least 17 August 2026; current guidance and grant conditions require councils to use Share for safeguarding, accommodation, and reporting workflows, while a public MHCLG repository at commit 120e42a871937c2f8f34d1f84c24cd194791551b provides runnable source, automated tests, MIT-licensed MHCLG code custody, and release history through version 2.10.0. The same bounded record identifies Made Tech support and London-hosted cloud infrastructure and does not establish independent end-to-end migration assurance, a Palantir deletion certificate or residual-copy inventory, supplier-free or cloud-independent operation, affected-party governance, or independently reconciled savings and service performance.

locator: DLUHC accepted six months of free Palantir support, then directly awarded a twelve-month contract worth £4.5 million and a further twelve-month extension worth £5.5 million.
The emergency deployment did not receive ordinary pre-live testing and some local authorities found the original system confusing.
DLUHC acknowledged that it should plan to move away from Palantir because of perceived cost, while an early-2023 migration was deferred because of start-up, timing, and quality risks.

sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government Digital
locator: MHCLG began building Share in-house in summer 2024 and migrated three years of operational data.
The department reports delivery in September 2025, exit from the supplier contract, public control of system data and code, and millions of pounds in annual running-cost savings.
The delivery account reports continual releases after launch and continuing work by a multidisciplinary public-service team.

sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
locator: Sponsor and guest data are stored in Share and council users must register to access the service.
Councils use Share for sponsor contact, accommodation and safeguarding checks, and daily or otherwise regular data updates.
The page was updated on 15 September 2025 to reflect the replacement Share system.

sources.authority: Secretary of State for the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
locator: Grant conditions require relevant Homes for Ukraine data to be entered on Share regularly and at least weekly.
Section 151 officers must sign off quarterly returns to the department.
The department reserves the right to recover funding where grant conditions are breached.

sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government and Home Office
locator: MHCLG and the Home Office are controllers for the Homes for Ukraine scheme.
Made Tech assists with support for the MHCLG-owned Share platform, which is hosted on cloud infrastructure in London.
The notice states that no decision about individuals will be made solely by automated decision making.

sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government public GitHub organisation
locator: The unarchived public repository main branch records a verified 17 August 2026 maintenance commit removing obsolete deduplication code.
The main branch is protected and requires the Build & Test check.
The commit supplies an immutable tree for the bounded public-code observation.

sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government public GitHub organisation
locator: The repository documents a runnable Django service with Poetry and Docker workflows and PostgreSQL persistence.
The repository documents AWS and S3 integration, local emulation, unit and integration tests, and Playwright browser tests.
The README establishes usable source and development capability rather than source-code escrow alone.

sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government public GitHub organisation
locator: The MIT licence records 2026 copyright in the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.
The licence permits use, modification, distribution, sublicensing, and sale subject to retention of the copyright and permission notice.

sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government public GitHub organisation
locator: Version 2.10.0 was released on 13 August 2026 and added initial Playwright configuration and browser tests.
The release history records continuing feature work, deduplication corrections, authentication and observability changes, and a cryptography vulnerability update during July and August 2026.
The changelog establishes repeated post-launch modification rather than a launch-only custody claim.

assessment.evidence_tier: Official audit, departmental delivery and operating records, statutory grant conditions, a central privacy notice, and immutable source-native public Git objects.
assessment.venue: United Kingdom National Audit Office, Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, GOV.UK, the public MHCLG GitHub organisation, issue 345, and the M-05 admission gate.
assessment.target: The boundary between completed supplier exit and durable public operating sovereignty with residual custody, remedy, successor, governance, and value controls.
assessment.upside: The record joins a named incumbent dependency to a completed in-house replacement, multi-year migration, live public workflow, public code custody, active maintenance, and continued statutory operating use.
assessment.downside: The replacement still relies on Made Tech support and London-hosted cloud infrastructure, while independent migration assurance, residual Palantir custody, deletion, service-quality, total-cost, and affected-person governance records remain unpublished.
assessment.failure_mode: Treating supplier-contract exit, public source code, official delivery claims, active releases, or continued use as proof of complete residual-custody reconciliation, supplier-free operation, democratic governance, or independently measured public value.
